tagline: Textron is a multi-industry company leveraging a global network of aircraft, defense, industrial and finance businesses to provide innovative solutions and services across commercial and government markets.
hero_kpi_rationale: 8% growth in 2025 with revenues reaching $14.8 billion, driven by demand in civil aviation and military defense programs (MV-75, Bell Aviation, Textron Aviation).

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned by the company over the year.
kpis.description: Revenue increased 8% in 2025, driven by Bell and Textron Aviation. Indicator tracked annually by company analysts, historical values over the last 13 years.
kpis.signal: Strong double-digit growth in aviation and defense.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after paying direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin declined slightly to 17.8% in 2025 versus 18.0% in 2024.

kpis.name: R&D Investments as % of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Share of revenue invested in research and development.
kpis.description: R&D expenses totaled $521 million in 2025, representing 3.5% of revenue (521/14799).

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Calculated from operating income (revenue - cost of sales - administrative expenses - R&D): (14799 - 12104 - 1173 - 521) / 14799 = 10.2%.
kpis.signal: Operating margin stable despite increased costs.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending to purchase or improve physical assets.
kpis.description: Typical sector estimate for aerospace-defense based on operational profile.
kpis.signal: Moderate CAPEX in industrial and aviation.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: Estimate based on public data (not documented in provided 10-K excerpt).

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $18.13 billion in latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of $3.88 billion in latest year

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned by the company over the year.
kpis.description: Revenue of $14.8 billion in 2025, up 8% driven by Bell (+$703M) and Textron Aviation (+$671M).

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after paying direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin at 17.8% in 2025, down 20 basis points.

risks.title: Cyberattacks
risks.score_rationale: The company implements numerous measures to protect its IT assets, but cyberattacks remain an existential threat. (Item 1A, p. 17)

risks.title: Regulations
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict regulations, particularly regarding national security and environmental protection. (Item 1A, p. 18)

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a competitive environment, notably in aviation and defense sectors. (Item 7, p. 20)

risks.title: Dependence on Government Demand
risks.score_rationale: The company heavily depends on government demand, particularly for defense products and services. Approximately 27% of 2025 revenues come from US government contracts. (Item 7, p. 21)

risks.title: Supplier Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company depends on suppliers for its operations, and supplier risks can negatively impact the supply chain. (Item 1A, p. 19)

risks.title: Reputation Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company may be exposed to reputation risks, notably in case of regulatory non-compliance or quality issues. (Item 1A, p. 18)

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related technologies is present in the company's 10-K document.
